title: THE DEFINING INDIA FACT — the sources exist and were never cited: 9.0% ref density, and PNGRB's own register is cited on 1 of 35 operating rows
summary: India gas is the inverse of Pakistan. Pakistan's problem was that no text existed behind a bulk map load; India's rows are real, coherent, actively maintained trunk lines whose numbers demonstrably come from the regulator — they were just never cited. Only 149 of 1,650 [ref] cells are filled (9.0%, 22 ref columns x 75 rows). PNGRB appears in 98 of those 149 filled cells, but they are concentrated on 29 in-development/cancelled rows: of the 35 OPERATING rows, exactly ONE carries a PNGRB reference. That is the gap this pass targets. RESOLUTION IN THIS PACKET: the PNGRB NGPL MIS register (https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, printed p.2 'PHYSICAL PROGRESS REPORT OF NATURAL GAS PIPELINE') is a monthly line-wise inventory giving entity, authorisation date, authorised length, authorised + design capacity (MMSCMD), operating length, under-construction length, target completion and states traversed. staging/register-crosswalk/ stages 151 units off it, 151/151 REFS_ADDED, all ref-only with NO value changes. TWO CAVEATS A REVIEWER MUST CARRY: (1) it covers COMMON-CARRIER pipelines only — dedicated and tie-in lines (ONGC trunk lines, Duliajan-Numaligarh, refinery feeders, regional networks) are inside its grand totals but are NOT itemised, so absence from the table is not evidence of anything; (2) INDEPENDENCE — GEM's India CapacityBcm/y reproduces PNGRB's authorised MMSCMD x 365 / 1000 to 2dp on ~20 rows, so PNGRB is very likely the ORIGIN of the sheet values rather than an independent check on them, and a company annual report restating the same authorised figure is the same origin again. Corroboration tiers in this packet were set with that in mind.

title: Operator is blank on 74 of 75 India gas rows — a genuine country gap, NOT the tracker norm
summary: The operators/owners tab (GID 1489950650) records an Operator on exactly ONE of India's 75 gas rows, while Owner1 is filled on 70. Across the whole GGIT gas tab, Operator is filled on 794 of 4,356 rows (18.2%); tracker-wide across both trackers it is 1,450 of 6,459 (22.4%). India at 1.3% is far below that, so this is a real country-level omission and not the ordinary sparse-column pattern. It generated the single largest flag class in the handoff worklist (39 of 61 rows). CORRECTION LOGGED: an earlier draft of this figure said 1.0% tracker-wide, which came from reading the 'Operator [ref]' column instead of 'Operator' — the 18.2% figure is the correct one, and it reverses the conclusion. NOTE FOR THE REVIEWER: Operator and Owner are different facts here. Several of these lines are held by single-purpose JV vehicles (GIGL, GITL, IGGL, Pipeline Infrastructure Ltd) whose shareholders are not the operating entity, so an Owner value must not be copied into Operator.

title: GulfPub India crosses BOTH escalation gates — 84 reference-only additions (gate: >30) and 22 status conflicts on 74 matched rows = 29.7% (gate: >10%)
summary: The GulfPub reconciliation (staging/recon-gulfpub-20260810/) matched 74 GEM rows and returned 84 additions, 56 near-misses, 40 GEM-only rows and 22 status conflicts. Both standing escalation thresholds in CLAUDE.md are crossed. The additions trigage by disposition as 56 NEAR_MISS, 23 DISCOVERY_CANDIDATE, 5 FRAGMENT_OF_EXISTING — so the headline number is dominated by near-misses needing hand adjudication rather than by genuine missing pipelines, and the 23 discovery candidates must each be checked against an existing GEM row under another name (-> OtherEnglishNames) before any new row is created. The 29.7% status-conflict rate is the item that actually needs a decision: at that rate the question is whether GulfPub's India status vocabulary maps onto GEM's the way the manifest assumes, or whether GEM's India statuses are stale as a class. Do NOT auto-apply any of it — a single Tier-2 dataset never reaches green alone.

title: The OSM India run returned 1 overlap against 74 GEM rows — and this is NOT a matcher defect: it is a granularity mismatch, and no override should be applied
summary: staging/recon-osm-20260810/ produced 1 overlap, 1 near-miss, 74 gem_only and 60 additions from 61 reference routes. The standing rule says a near-null recon run is a claim about the matcher until its health line is read — so it was read, and the health line is CLEAN: 44.3% of reference records are named (India is the healthiest OSM extract in the registry so far, against Pakistan's 0% and Libya's 14%), 100% carry geometry, and 98.7% of the GEM pool is routed. No MATCH_QUALITY warning fired, and none should have. The real cause is GRANULARITY: India's OSM features are short fragments (median 7.4 km across the 60 additions, many under 1 km) of very long GEM trunk lines, and with geometry_weight at 0.45 a 97 km trace of a 1,104 km pipeline can score a perfect 1.00 on name and still land at 0.34-0.44 composite against a 0.45 yellow threshold. The composite distribution confirms it — max 0.5275, p90 0.3413, median 0.1877. The 34 FRAGMENT_OF_EXISTING records are the engine reaching the RIGHT answer by a different route, not evidence of a broken axis; most are unnamed sub-kilometre stubs inside the Gujarat grid area whose best guess is correctly P0927. CORRECTION LOGGED: an earlier draft of this escalation diagnosed a dead name axis and recommended a per-dataset geoarea_weight override for India. That was wrong on the evidence and the override must NOT be applied — sources/osm/manifest.yml deliberately carries no override for gas_in. What IS real: the 25 DISCOVERY_CANDIDATE records remain untriaged, and each must be matched against an existing GEM row under another name before any new row is created. Four GEM rows also gain LOCATION-only corroboration from perfectly name-matched fragments (P0934 KKBMPL 4 traces / 306 km, P0925 HVJ 106 km, P0915 Dabhol-Bangalore 4 traces / 70 km, P0929 JHBDPL 66 km) — partial coverage corroborates location, never length or extent.

title: Cluster A — the Bhatinda-Jammu-Srinagar corridor is double-counted: a foreclosed 725 km GIGL grant still carried alongside the three rows that replaced it
summary: P0908 is framed as a 725 km Bhatinda-Jammu-Srinagar grant to GAIL/GIGL that PNGRB foreclosed. The corridor is separately carried by P5533 (Bhatinda-Gurdaspur), P3913 and P5413 — so roughly 465-567 km of pipe is counted twice depending on which framing of P0908 is used. This is a length/asset double-count, not a naming duplicate, and it needs a human decision on which framing survives. The same cluster surfaced a DISCOVERY candidate as a by-product: a ~325 km Jammu-Srinagar re-tender for which no awardee could be found — that is a genuine gap in GEM coverage, not part of the double-count. Full record: staging/redundancy/, cluster A (4 rows, severity escalate).

title: Cluster B — P0907 Barauni-Guwahati is a double-counted SECTION of P0929 (JHBDPL), and its owner is wrong
summary: P0907 (Barauni-Guwahati, 718 km) is a section of the Jagdishpur-Haldia-Bokaro-Dhamra pipeline carried by P0929, whose PNGRB authorisation name literally embeds the Barauni-Guwahati leg. Two separate defects follow: the length is counted twice, and P0907's Owner appears to have been copied from the adjacent row P0906 (AGCL) when the authorisation holder is GAIL. Also settled in this cluster: P1309 (IGGL) is explicitly NOT part of JHBDPL and must not be folded in. Full record: staging/redundancy/, cluster B (3 rows, severity escalate).

title: Cluster C — one system capacity (107.00 MMSCMD) is stamped on five different HVJ/DVPL/GREP rows
summary: P0925 (HVJ), P0919 (DVPL-I), P3298 (DVPL-II), P3297 (GREP-I) and P3299 (GREP-II) all carry Capacity = 107.00 MMSCMD. These are a mix of series and parallel segments of one system, so no single number can be correct for all five: a series segment's throughput is not the system's, and two parallel loops do not each carry the system total. PNGRB reports HVJ + GREP + DVPL + VDPL as ONE combined authorised asset (6,169 km authorised / 6,732 km operating), which is why the number propagated. GEM's five-row split is a legitimate granularity choice and should NOT be collapsed — but the capacity column needs a per-segment answer or an explicit convention. Full record: staging/redundancy/, cluster C (5 rows, severity escalate).

title: Cluster F — Kanai Chhata is ONE PNGRB authorisation carried as two GEM rows (settled by diffing register editions)
summary: P2214 and the Kanai Chhata row trace to a single authorisation, PNGRB/Auth/2-NGPL/BID/KSPL/(8)/2019, held by HPPL, dated 08.07.2019, 317 km / 19.20 MMSCMD. The two rows look like different projects only because a 01-Aug-2022 amendment shifted the terminus from Shrirampur to Panitar; the authorisation number, sponsor and authorisation date are identical across register editions. A secondary defect: P2214's EndState = Maharashtra is a place-name collision, not a real terminus. This cluster is the cleanest demonstration of the method that works in India — duplicates here are REGULATORY, and the dispositive test is authorisation number / sponsor / authorisation date holding constant while the NAME changes, not name or endpoint similarity. Full record: staging/redundancy/, cluster F (2 rows, severity escalate).

title: P0934 (KKBMPL) states 44 km against three independent measurements of 306-675 km — the single strongest row-level finding of the pass
summary: Kochi-Koottanad-Bangalore-Mangalore is recorded at LengthKnownKm = 44.0. Three independent lines of evidence contradict it: the PNGRB register reports 675 km OPERATING, OSM has 306 km of the line mapped, and the row's own drawn geojson measures 375 km (an 8.53x length_ratio, the largest in the country). The three disagree with each other on extent — which is expected, since they measure the commissioned portion, the mapped portion and the drawn portion respectively — but all three exclude 44 km. The 44 likely records one early commissioned segment and was never updated as the line was progressively commissioned. Needs a sourced replacement value plus a decision on what the row's extent represents (phase, commissioned portion, or full authorisation), because the same question governs its phase-pair partner.

title: P5411 (Mehsana-Bhatinda Phase II) draws 2,317 km of geometry — more than both phases of the line combined — so the duplication is on the ROUTE side
summary: P5411 states 763 km and its geojson measures 2,317 km (3.04x). For scale, both Mehsana-Bhatinda phases together are 1,940 km, so the Phase II geometry alone exceeds the whole line. This is the exact INVERSE of cluster A: there the values double-count and the geometry is fine; here the values look right and the drawn route double-counts. It is a routes-repo defect, not a sheet defect, and it must not be 'fixed' by editing LengthKnownKm to match the drawing. Related: P3334 (Digha-Contai) draws 599 km against a stated 115 km (5.21x) — close to the 705 km STATED length of P0913 (Contai-Paradip-Dattapulia), i.e. the 115 km feeder appears to have been drawn with its neighbour's extent. That supports cluster J's reading that the H-Energy West Bengal / Digha rows have entangled identities.

title: Diameter is recorded on 10 of 75 India gas rows, and the regulator's register cannot fix it
summary: Only 10 of 75 rows carry a Diameter, and the PNGRB NGPL MIS table — the document that resolves length, capacity, status and authorisation holder — does NOT include diameter at all. So unlike every other gap in this country, this one has no single-document answer. Diameters live in PNGRB bid and tender documents (pngrb.gov.in/pdf/ngp/bid/...), authorisation letters, and entity maps and annual reports from GAIL, GSPL and IOCL, i.e. one document per project. A sourced diameter is correspondingly high-value here. One live defect in the class: P0906 (Assam Regional Gas Network) records diameters of '350, 400, 500, 800', which are plainly millimetres in a column that expects inches — confirm the intended figures from a source rather than converting blind.

title: Five of eleven redundancy clusters REFUTE a duplicate hypothesis — recorded deliberately so the next sweep does not re-raise them
summary: Clusters D, G, H, I and K each looked like a textbook duplicate on name alone and each survived scrutiny as two or more genuinely distinct assets: D (Langtala trio — three owners, three destinations off one gas field; the real defect is P2215's MMcf/d units), G (Kakinada-Srikakulam — P6538 is PNGRB's Jan-2024 suo-motu SUCCESSOR at 20 MMSCMD, not a restatement of the cancelled P0932; this one was drafted as a probable merge and REVERSED on the 4.5x capacity gap), H (Gujarat grids — GAIL vs GSPL, two companies), I (HUT vs MUT — CAG Report No. 21 of 2016 names both and reports a 3.09% metering discrepancy between them), K (P2752 vs P1434 — IMC authorisation 19.02.2018, 667 km, already tracked). Cluster E's four phase pairs also reconcile to the register, with ONE exception: P5533 + P3913 sum to 392 km against the register's 261 km. An unrecorded refutation gets re-raised by the next sweep, which is why these are staged as findings rather than dropped.
